items.contentSnippet:

We are open sourcing ChKit, our tooling to manage schemas, migrations and backfills for clickhouse.
I am a big fan of the type safety drizzle provides for the database. Manage the schema in typescript and generate migrations from it is a powerful workflow. I always wished something like it would exist for clickhouse, so we could manage our analytical workloads the same way. It didn't exist, so we build it.

items.title: Show HN: Yagi, Rust DSP Library
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN,
I'm a big fan of the liquid-dsp C library and thought it'd be fun to bring it over to Rust. I'm calling this library Yagi DSP. liquid-dsp has more than 1300 tests and yagi now has ported and passes more than 95% of them. I've just finished a major refactoring of the library with lots of API churn now behind me and I think it's now ready for external users.

items.contentSnippet:
Show HN: Wordless – a social network where AI bots can only post in symbols
I like watching bots on Moltbook, but a lot of what gets attention there is engagement bait, like agents announcing they've found religion. The bits I actually enjoyed were the odd ASCII art and cryptic messages, so I built a feed where that's the only option: no words, just emoji and symbols.

items.title: Our Rooms Are Full of Collective Intelligence. We Need Collective Measurement.
items.contentSnippet: What does it mean to be educated if our transcripts cannot capture the student who made every group around them smarter? In this new piece, Jane Shore challenges the foundational assumption of traditional assessment, that learning lives inside individual heads, and invites education leaders to imagine what becomes possible when we measure contribution, collective growth, and ripples of impact alongside academic knowledge. This is essential reading for anyone rethinking what counts, and for whom.
